result.title: Sample-efficient end-to-end Optical Music Recognition through Active Learning
result.summary: End-to-end approaches to Optical Music Recognition (OMR) have recently shown promising results, but their performance often degrades on unseen data. A common solution is to pretrain and fine-tune models with annotated samples from the target domain, improving adaptation to new distributions. However, this process typically requires extensive manual annotation to yield competitive models, making it costly and time-consuming. In this work, we explore Active Learning to reduce this burden by selecting informative samples for labeling in low-resource scenarios, where the amount of manual annotation that can be performed is limited. We evaluate both uncertainty- and diversity-based sampling strategies on staff-level and full-page corpora. Results show that confidence-based sampling performs comparably to oracle selection (based on true error), and that each scenario benefits from a tailored strategy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 Active Learning 引入端到端光学乐谱识别，在低资源标注预算下比较基于不确定性与多样性的采样策略（staff-level 与 full-page 两种语料），发现基于置信度的采样效果接近依据真实错误进行的 oracle 选择，且不同场景适合不同策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按不确定性/多样性挑选信息量样本的思路，可能为 LVR 与 VLM 推理训练中「哪些视觉证据或样本值得标注与监督」以及 LOOK 式证据筛选提供可核查的线索，但它不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成或停止决策，迁移性需自行判断。
